summary: Backend-only (Node engine js/bulk-esim/core.js, simulated Spenza). With nodejs STOPPED: test_bulk_esim_engine 39/39, test_bulk_esim_autoscale 25/25, test_bulk_esim_stop_upload_iter239 86/86. With nodejs STARTED: test_bulk_esim_bot_flow all steps OK ('booking scheduled 510 51 wallet'). Independent suite js/tests/test_bulk_esim_autoscale_iter241.js: 21/21 requested checks (a-g) pass. 6 bug probes for double-buy, stale forecast and stuck bookings all reproduced the bug (P1-P6). These only matter when autoProvision=true and manualApproval=false, which is not the default. Regression (STOP, refunds, Caribbean/toll-free, 500-2000 parts, $0.10/$0.15, quiet hours) is covered by the passing suites. /bulk output (bot.js:171-173) shows forecast, today/tomorrow capacity, per-line today/cap and auto-buy state.

critical.issue: P1 reproduced. If payment arrives after holdUntil, reservedBySlot() skips the booking because it is still awaiting_payment with an expired hold. linesShort() then leaves out the booking's own volume, so short=0. The booking becomes 'scheduled' with 0 lines bought (1000 SMS, 0 eSIMs), even though the re-check used projected lines to accept it. Fix: compute short after setBooking, or pass the booking's own allocation into linesShort.

P2 reproduced: double-buy. Two bookings on the same date were paid at the same time (Promise.all). Each linesShort() counted both bookings before any purchase existed, so 16 lines were bought when 8 were needed. The same race happens between a bot-process confirm and the leader's autoscale, and the maxEsims check in provisionOne can also be passed by both. Fix: use a Mongo lock (e.g. lock('provision')) around 'compute short and provisionMany' in both confirmBooking and autoscale, and recompute short inside the lock.

P3 reproduced. The credit reserve is checked against state.forecast, which is only refreshed by creditWatch every 2 minutes, and nothing inside a batch subtracts what was just spent. With forecast.available=$15 and a $10 line, provisionMany(4) bought 4 lines ($40). Fix: cap provisionMany at buyable(c), or reduce the forecast by the cost of each line bought.

P4 reproduced. fleet() only counts purchasing/provisioning/testing lines from tomorrow on (ahead>=1). On the booking day, lines that are bought but not yet active (live provisioning without an msisdn, or a new number still in its delivery test) count as 0. Autoscale then buys again: 16 extra lines on top of 4 pending for a 1000-SMS booking. The new lines are on warm-up day 1 (80 texts each), so the shortfall is large, and it repeats every 30 min until maxEsims or the budget is reached. Fix: count pending lines on day 0 for the shortfall calculation (not for selling), or skip lines already bought for that booking.

minor.issue: P5 reproduced. Every refusal for capacity or slot is recorded in bsDemand, including bookings for past dates (d(-1) recorded 2000), past or full hours (err_slot), and dates beyond the window. unmetDemand() adds up all of it whatever the date and adds it to every future day >= leadDays, so typos or retries can drive line purchases. Fix: record only dates >= leadDays (or the 7-day window) and only real capacity refusals, and use each demand's own date in autoscale.

P6 reproduced. A refused booking leaves a bsDemand row. If the same customer then books the same volume and date successfully, the row stays and autoscale buys for the booking and the stale demand again (confirm bought 4, autoscale bought +4). Fix: delete bsDemand `${cid}:${date}` on a successful createBooking or confirmBooking.

Projected lines are valued at lineCap(ahead+1), which assumes they are bought now. If the purchase only happens later (confirm failed on credit or budget, so autoscale buys on day-1 or day 0), the lines have a much lower warm-up cap on the booking day. The booking can then go over the real per-day capacity, and texts spill into the 2-day expiry/refund path.

If provisionMany buys only part of the lines (budget, credit or maxEsims) and lines never arrive, a volume-only booking (no campaignId) stays 'provisioning' forever: autoscale only moves it when linesShort==0, and finishCampaigns never touches it. The customer gets no notice or refund for the missing capacity.

When the daily auto-replace limit is reached, the line stays 'suspended'. healthCheck never re-checks status 'suspended', so a line the provider un-suspends never returns to the pool. It also never gets auto-replaced on later days.

The per-line counter uses today() (UTC midnight) while the customer quota uses dayKey(resetHourUtc). They drift apart if resetHourUtc != 0. bsConfig also collects one row per day (creditwarn:*, replaces:*, scale:*, provcredit:*) with no TTL.

action_items: Fix P1: in confirmBooking, include the booking's own allocation in linesShort when the hold has expired (or compute short after the status change).
Fix P2: put a shared lock around shortfall computation and purchase in confirmBooking and autoscale, and recheck maxEsims inside the lock.
Fix P3: cap provisionMany at buyable(c), or reduce the in-memory forecast.available by each line's cost.
Fix P4: count lines already bought/pending for today's bookings in autoscale's shortfall (avoid re-buying every 30 min).
Fix P5/P6: record bsDemand only for real capacity refusals on dates >= leadDays within 7 days, clear it when that cid:date is booked, and apply demand per date.
Handle bookings stuck in 'provisioning' (notify, refund, or move to scheduled at startAt) and re-check 'suspended' lines that were never replaced.
critical_code_review_comments: core.js is 617 lines of very dense one-liners. Several functions (healthCheck, processOne, overview) each pack more than 5 statements into one line, which makes race review hard.
Purchases are not idempotent across processes: no lock or idempotency on 'need N lines for date X'.
creditShort/buyable rely on a forecast snapshot that can be up to 2 minutes old; the forecast does not include unpaid holds or lines just bought.

success_rate.backend: 100% of requested checks (171/171 incl. suites); 6/6 bug probes reproduced

seed_data_creation: None kept. My suite wipes bs* collections (incl. bsEsimDaily, bsDemand) at start and end, as the existing suites do. Customers prefixed TEST_Iter241.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run engine suites with nodejs stopped, then start nodejs for bot_flow. test_bulk_esim_autoscale_iter241.js prints '🐞 BUG [probe]' lines for P1-P6; after fixes they should print '🟢 ok'. P4 simulates the booking day by moving the booking date/allocation to today and setting lines back to provisioning. nodejs was restarted and is RUNNING at the end.
